what: Huntington Bancshares is a regional bank headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, serving households and businesses across the Midwest and, after recent acquisitions, the Southwest. It has been lending since 1866.
customers: Midwestern households and small businesses, commercial borrowers, and specialty finance customers nationally.
money: deposits, mortgages, car and recreational vehicle lending
corporate lending, treasury management and specialty finance
moat: Deposit share built over 150 years in Ohio and Michigan, which funds lending cheaply, plus niche lending businesses such as equipment and fund finance.
risks: Commercial property lending is a watched area across regional banking
Integrating recent acquisitions including Cadence is a large undertaking
Deposit costs rise when savers move money to higher-yielding accounts
Midwestern economic growth is slower than the Sunbelt
opportunities: Revenue grew about 11% last year with a 27% net margin
Expansion into Texas and the Southwest adds faster-growing markets
Analysts see about 25% upside from current levels
watch: Net interest margin, loan growth, and integration of the Cadence acquisition.
